answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit bids, with rewards weighted by time locked and slashed for provable double-spending. This does not prove a unique person is behind each agent; it makes fake identities costly because every Sybil must tie up real capital and risk losing it. A garden of identities may look convincing in the mirror, but its pulse still depends on the attacker’s budget.
